title: Illustration and Iconography Don’ts
slide_intent: Separate retired and current assets so viewers encounter one coherent visual identity rather than a mixture of eras.
strategic_value: Explicitly retiring older product, claims, stripe and promotional graphics can protect the consistency of Burger King’s new system.
demonstration: Four crossed-out panels show previous product icons, claims badges, textured stripes and promotional graphics beside a note against mixing old and new identities.
practical_value: Check whether a proposed illustration belongs to the retired system before placing it in the new identity.

content_islands.name: Retirement explanation
content_islands.spec: Place the consistency rationale and explanation of old examples at left.

content_islands.name: Product and claims examples
content_islands.spec: Show crossed-out product silhouettes and claims badges across the top.

content_islands.name: Stripe and promotion examples
content_islands.spec: Show crossed-out textured stripes and promotional marks beneath, retaining each prohibition caption.

reference_purposes.Intent: The copy explicitly links the prohibition to consistency throughout the visual identity.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The page prohibits using the shown product icons, claims icons, stripes and promotional icons from the previous identity.

ingredient.name: Retired illustration assets
ingredient.role: Prevent visual mixing between the previous and new identities.
ingredient.application: Do not use the previous product icons, claims icons, stripes or promotional icons shown.
ingredient.scope: Historical transition rule in the 2020 guide; crossed-out examples are rejected assets, not current expression specimens.
